title: Broccoli Bread Quiche
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 18
description: Healthy quiche with whole grain bread crust.

ingredients.item: beaten eggs (or equivalent no cholesterol egg substitute)

instructions.text: Toast bread lightly, cut each slice in half. Arrange bread slices in a small non-stick baking pan.
Layer broccoli on top. Stir yogurt into eggs until blended, then spoon over broccoli.
Sprinkle with nutmeg, salt and lemon pepper.
Bake, uncovered, in a preheated oven at 350 degrees for 60 minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean.

title: Mu Shu Pork in Pita Bread
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 20
description: Asian-inspired pork stir-fry served in pita bread.

ingredients.item: pork chops, cut into strips (1 1/2 to 2 inches long)

instructions.text: Mix pork, cornstarch, water, and soy sauce. Cut onions into 2 pieces then into thin strips.
Heat wok or skillet until very hot, pour in 1 tablespoon oil then add eggs. Cook until dry, break cooked eggs up into small pieces. Put on plate.
Reheat wok and pour in remaining oil, add onions then stir-fry for 30 seconds. Add the pork and stir-fry until it changes color and separates into strips (if meat sticks, add more oil).
Add cabbage and salt, stir-fry 2 more minutes. Add eggs, stir until all is heated through. In pita bread spread hoisin sauce, then fill.

title: Pocket Bread
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 20
description: Homemade pita/pocket bread.

instructions.text: Dissolve yeast in warm water. Add salt and mix well.
Let rise and shape into pockets. Bake until puffed.

title: Haystack Chocolate Pancakes
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 34
description: Chocolate pancakes topped with coconut-pecan topping and strawberry fluff.

instructions.text: Prepare coconut-pecan topping. Combine evaporated milk, sugar, egg yolks, butter, vanilla, flaked coconut, and chopped pecans. Cook over medium heat until thickened.
Prepare pancakes with milk, eggs and vegetable oil according to package directions for 2 cups mix. Preheat griddle.
Using scant 1/4 cup batter for each pancake, cook over medium-high heat 2 to 3 minutes or until underside is browned and surface is bubbly.
Serve with warm Coconut-Pecan topping. Makes 16 to 18 servings.

title: German Oven Pancakes
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 34
description: Puffy oven-baked pancakes with fruit topping.

instructions.text: Combine and set aside. Heat to very warm, 2 cups milk and 1/4 c. oleo - then add above mixture.
Beat 3 eggs slightly and add; beat until smooth; this can be refrigerated up to 4 days but after 2 days, add 2 more tablespoons sugar, makes 10 to 12.

title: Caramel Ring
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 36
description: Sweet caramel pull-apart bread using Pillsbury biscuits.

instructions.text: Mix and pat together in bottom of large ring mold. 1/3 c. butter, melted, 3/4 c. white sugar.
Mix together sugar and cinnamon. Dip each biscuit in butter, then in sugar mixture, covering the entire biscuit.
Stand on edge in mold. Bake at 375 degrees for 30 minutes. Nuts can be added to first mixture.
Can be made ahead and held in refrigerator for 1/2 day.

title: Overnight Coffee Cake
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 36
description: Make-ahead coffee cake with frozen dough balls.

instructions.text: Combine dry pudding mix with brown sugar and pecans. Place frozen dough balls in well greased bundt pan. Pour melted butter over dough so each ball is coated.
Sprinkle pudding mixture over dough balls. Place in freezer overnight. Remove from freezer and bake at 350 degrees until golden brown for 45 to 50 minutes. Invert on plate and serve.

title: Granola Cereal
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 40
description: Homemade granola with oats, nuts, and dried fruit.

instructions.text: Combine (except raisins) in a large bowl. Then combine: 1/2 c. (each) honey, oil, water, 1 tsp (each) salt, vanilla.
Add to dry ingredients; mix well. Spread in two 10x15 pans that have been sprayed with Pam. Bake 1 hour at 250 degrees, stirring every 15 minutes.
The last 15 minutes, mix in the raisins evenly and turn off the oven; remove pans and let cool before storing in an airtight container. Serve with milk; no sugar.

title: Waffles
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 40
description: Basic waffle recipe that can be made ahead.

instructions.text: Combine and set aside. Heat to very warm, 2 cups milk and 1/4 c. oleo - then add above mixture.
Beat 3 eggs slightly and add; beat until smooth; this can be refrigerated up to 4 days but after 2 days, add 2 more tablespoons sugar, makes 10 to 12.

title: Wagon Wheel Sausage Pie - Breakfast
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 40
description: Hearty breakfast pie with sausage, hash browns, and cream cheese.

instructions.text: Brown sausage and set aside. Prepare hash browns according to package.
Combine ingredients and bake until set.

title: Baked Spanish Potato Omelet
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 42
description: Spanish-style potato omelet baked in the oven.

instructions.text: Beat eggs until fluffy. Fold in remaining ingredients. Spray a round, non-stick cake pan with 25 to 30 minutes until no-fat frying.
Spoon in omelet mixture. Bake at 350 degrees for 25-30 minutes until eggs are set. Cut into wedges.
The cooked ham can be replaced with leftover roast poultry, seafood or water packed tuna.

title: Mushroom Quiche
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 44
description: Rich mushroom quiche with Swiss cheese.

instructions.text: Prepare mushrooms with 2 tablespoons minced scallions. Cook in 3 tablespoons butter. Stir in wine if desired. Mix cream.
Stir in teaspoon salt and 1 teaspoon lemon juice. Pour mushrooms in the cream and egg mixture.
Pour mixture and eggs together. Pour into partially baked pie shell. Sprinkle with cheese and dot with butter. Bake at 375 degrees for 25 to 30 minutes.

title: Cottage Cheese Pancakes
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 44
description: Light and fluffy pancakes made with cottage cheese.

instructions.text: Beat the eggs with fructose and salt. Add cottage cheese, milk and beat until smooth.
Stir in melted butter. Add flour and beat until smooth.
Turn when lightly browned and brown on other side. Serve with hot syrup. Makes 12 pancakes.

title: Roadrunners Rice and Eggs
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 44
description: Quick and easy breakfast with rice, eggs, and cheese.

instructions.text: Cook rice as directed, drain any excess liquid. Put into frying pan and pour beaten eggs over the top of rice.
Begin to scramble egg and add cheese until done. NOTE: Cook rice the night before it makes a real quick easy breakfast. NOTE: Also you can add some turkey ham or chicken.

title: Critter's French Toast
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 46
description: Crispy French toast with Bran Flakes coating.

instructions.text: Combine eggs, milk, salt and vanilla in shallow dish. Dip bread into mixture, turning well and allowing time for both sides to absorb liquid and place in a single layer on a well greased baking sheet.
Drizzle with butter. Bake in 450 degree oven about 10 minutes or until brown. Serve with warm maple syrup or honey butter. Serves 3.

title: Stuffed Eggs
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 46
description: Deviled eggs with turkey ham.

instructions.text: Cut eggs in half lengthwise, remove yolks, mash. Add remaining ingredients and pack into whites.

title: Fish Omelet
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 46
description: Protein-rich omelet with halibut or other fish.

instructions.text: Make a cream sauce with first 3 ingredients and seasonings and add fish well mashed.
Beat eggs and mix lightly with fish. Bake in mold, covered with oiled paper over pan of hot water for 1 1/2 hours.

title: Fudd's Blueberry Pancakes
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 46
description: Fluffy pancakes with fresh blueberries and honey.

instructions.text: Mix ingredients and cook on griddle. Add blueberries to batter before cooking.

title: Cheese Grits
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 50

instructions.text: Add grits to boiling water. Boil 2-3 minutes. Turn off heat. Add the remaining ingredients. Pour in greased casserole dish. Sprinkle with paprika. Bake 30 minutes at 350 degrees. Serves 6.

title: Layered Eggs
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 50

instructions.text: Trim the crust from the bread. Toast the bread. With a cookie cutter, cut circles. Line a 9 x 13 inch pan with the bread scraps.
Layer the Monterey Jack, cooked spinach, ham, mushrooms, and the toast circles. Mix eggs, milk, onion, salt and dry mustard. Pour over the circles to soak them.
Sprinkle with Cheddar cheese. Cover. Let stand overnight. Bake at 325 degrees for 55 minutes. Serves 12.

title: Brunch Souffle
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 51

ingredients.item: slices bread, cut into 1/4 inch cubes

instructions.text: Prepare night before. Brown sausage - drain. Spread in 9x13x2 pan. Beat eggs. Blend in milk, mustard, salt, bread cubes and cheese. Pour mixture over sausage. Cover pan and refrigerate overnight.
Uncover and bake at 350 degrees for about one hour.

title: Huevos Rancheros with Green Chili Sauce
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 53

instructions.text: Saute pork until cooked through. Add onion and butter. Add remaining ingredients.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 1 hour. Thicken with flour and water as needed.
For 8 servings: Heat 2 flour tortillas and top each with 1 egg cooked as desired. Cover with green chili sauce and sprinkle with shredded Cheddar cheese.

title: Brunch Enchiladas
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 53

instructions.text: Combine ham, onions, green pepper. Spoon about 1/3 cup mixture onto each tortilla and roll up.
Place seam side down in greased 11x17 baking dish. Mix eggs, cream, flour, salt, garlic and Tabasco. Pour over tortillas.
Cover and chill overnight. Bake uncovered at 350 degrees for 45-50 minutes. Sprinkle with cheese last 5 minutes.

title: Curried Fruit
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 55

instructions.text: Layer above in order in a 2 quart oblong pan (greased). Bake 45 minutes at 300 degrees.

Heat oven to 325 degrees. Drain fruits well. In small pot, melt butter, add sugar and curry. Place fruits in a 1 1/2 quart casserole. Pour the butter mixture over all. Mix well. Bake 1 hour uncovered. Excellent with ham or lamb. 12 servings.

title: Fruit Mold with Yogurt
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 55

instructions.text: Dissolve Jello in boiling water. Add all fruit and juices. Pour half into large mold and set. Spread with yogurt. Pour remaining Jello mixture over and chill until firm.

title: Cinnamon Coffee Bar
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 55

instructions.text: Mix shortening and sugar. Add egg and coffee. Blend dry ingredients and add to mixture. Spread in greased pan. Bake at 350 degrees. Top with powdered sugar glaze.

title: Benedictine Sandwich
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 59

instructions.text: Grate cucumbers and drain well. Grate onion. Blend these into cream cheese and add enough mayo to make a soft spread. Season lightly and add drops of coloring to make a delicate green. Makes 1 1/2 cups. Great for finger sandwiches or stuffing tomatoes/mushrooms.

title: Seafood Luncheon Dish
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 59

instructions.text: Combine ingredients placing shrimp on top. Bake 1 hour at 350 degrees. Serve with sauce: 1 can cream of mushroom soup plus 1/3 cup milk, heated.

title: Maridadi Eggs
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 61

instructions.text: Spread one side of each slice of toast with softened butter. Beat the egg whites with salt until stiff but not dry. Mound the beaten whites on top of the 6 toast slices.

With a spoon, carefully lift one egg yolk and press into the center of the mounded egg whites. Bake in a very hot oven (475 degrees) for 4 to 6 minutes until meringues are lightly browned. Serve immediately. Makes 3 to 6 servings.

title: Crab Breakfast Casserole
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 61

instructions.text: Mix all ingredients. Place in a greased 9 x 9 inch casserole dish and let set in refrigerator overnight.
Remove from refrigerator 1 hour before baking. Bake in a 325 degree oven for 1 hour.

title: Fruit Pizza
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 63

ingredients.item: Pillsbury's Best Sugar Cookie Dough (20 oz)

instructions.text: Freeze dough for one hour. Line a 14 inch pizza pan with foil. Slice dough 1/8 inch thick and line pan, overlap slices but don't flatten into pan.
Bake at 375 degrees for 12 minutes or until browned. Cool completely. Invert crust onto another pan, remove foil, put it back on the same pizza pan.
Combine cream cheese, sugar, and vanilla until blended. Spread on crust, arrange fruit. Put preserves and water in bowl and stir to glaze-like consistency. Pour over fruit; chill.

title: Lemony Poppy Seed Bread
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 63

instructions.text: Heat oven to 350 degrees. Using solid shortening, grease and flour bottom only of 9"x5" loaf pan.
In large bowl, blend all ingredients at low speed until moistened. Beat 2 minutes at medium speed. Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake at 325 degrees for 50 to 60 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean. Cool 15 minutes; remove from pan. Wrap tightly and store in refrigerator. Yield: 1 loaf.

title: Skillet Orange Coffee Cake
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 67

ingredients.item: Pillsbury's best all purpose or unbleached flour

instructions.text: Heat oven to 350 degrees. Grease 10" oven proof skillet. Lightly spoon flour into measuring cup, level off.
In large bowl, combine flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. In small bowl, combine orange juice, oil and eggs; add to dry ingredients, mixing well.
Pour batter into prepared skillet. In small bowl, combine bread crumbs, sugar, cinnamon, margarine and orange peel with fork until crumbly. Sprinkle topping evenly over batter.
Bake at 350 degrees for 25 to 30 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes; serve warm. 12 servings.

title: Mini Cheesecakes
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 68

instructions.text: Line muffin tin with foil cupcake liners. Place 1 vanilla wafer in each liner. Mix cream cheese, vanilla and sugar on medium speed until well blended. Add eggs and mix well.

Pour over wafers, filling each one almost full. Bake 25 minutes at 325 degrees. Remove from muffin pan when cool. Chill. Top with fruit, preserves, nuts or chocolate. These are quick and easy and can be cooled quickly in freezer.

title: Peanut Butter Cake
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 68

instructions.text: Prepare pans. Cream shortening. Add slowly and beat in 1 cup brown sugar and peanut butter. In another bowl, beat together 2 eggs and 1/2 cup brown sugar. Add this to the first mixture and beat well.

Sift together flour, salt and powder. Add dry ingredients alternately to first mixture with 1 cup milk with vanilla. Pour mixture into pans and bake at once until firm in center. Bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes.

title: Mexican Fruit Cake
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 72

instructions.text: Hand mix only. Bake one hour and 10 minutes. Comes out very moist. Makes a big cake. Very good.

CAKE: Mix all ingredients in large mixing bowl. Stir by hand until completely mixed. Pour into greased and floured 13 x 9 inch baking pan or dish. Bake 40 to 45 minutes in metal pan, 30 to 35 minutes in glass baking dish. ICING: Mix together. Ice when cake is cool.

title: Mountain Cake
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 72

instructions.text: Separate eggs and reserve whites in small bowl. Beat egg yolks, add sugar gradually and beat. Add bread crumbs, nuts, farina, and baking powder one at a time, beating after each addition.
Beat egg white stiff and fold into mixture. Bake at 350 degrees for 40 minutes. When cool, crumble into several pieces. Before serving, fold cake into whipped cream.

Pile into mountain form and garnish with cherries. This can also be put in a child's sand pain and sprinkled with crushed Oreo cookies. Garnish with a plastic flower and use sand shovel as serving spoon.

title: Earthquake Cake
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 74

instructions.text: Combine the 1 cup of pecans and 1 cup of coconut and put in the bottom of a 9 x 13 inch baking pan.

Mix the German chocolate cake as directed on the box. Pour over the nuts and coconut. Over low heat, melt the margarine and cream cheese. Slowly stir in the entire box of confectioners sugar. Spoon cream cheese mixture over cake mix. Do not spread, just drop over top.
Bake cake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes.

title: Toll House Cup Cakes
source_note: F.B.C. of Jasmine Lakes Cookbook, page 74

instructions.text: Prepare graham cracker crust (20 graham crackers, 4 tablespoons sugar and 1/4 pound melted butter) and press into springform pan. Cream 1 pound of cream cheese, 2 eggs and 1 cup sugar. Pour mixture into crust and bake 30 minutes at 350 degrees. Cool 20 minutes.

Make top dressing using 1 pint sour cream, 4 tablespoons sugar and 1 teaspoon vanilla. Pour mixture over cooled cake and return to oven for 5 minutes at 500 degrees. After cake cools, refrigerate several hours before serving.

title: Crunchy Chocolate Malt Cupcakes
description: Tastes just like a Crunch bar.

instructions.text: Make the frosting: Sprinkle the sugar evenly in a dry saucepan and add the corn syrup. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring. Continue to boil, stirring, until the caramel is smooth, about 2 minutes.

Combine both chocolates and the salt in a bowl, then pour the hot caramel over. Slowly pour in the heavy cream, stirring constantly, until the caramel is smooth, about 5 minutes. Whisk until smooth and shiny, then cover and refrigerate until set, about 4 hours or overnight. (The frosting can be made up to 2 days ahead.)
Make the cupcakes: Position a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 375°. Line two 12-cup muffin pans with paper liners. Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt in a bowl until smooth.

Beat the sugar and butter in a third bowl with a mixer until light and fluffy, about 7 minutes. Add the malted milk powder, cocoa and vanilla; beat until combined. Add the eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition. With the mixer on low speed, add the flour mixture in three parts, alternating with the half-and-half in two parts, beginning and ending with flour.

Divide the batter evenly among the prepared cups, filling each about three-quarters of the way. Bake until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, 15 to 20 minutes. Let cool in the pans for 10 minutes, then transfer the cupcakes to a wire rack to cool completely.

Beat the chilled frosting with a mixer or whisk until thick, about 2 minutes, but don't overwhip. Spoon on the cupcakes or transfer to a pastry bag with a star tip and pipe on top. Refrigerate until ready to serve, then sprinkle with the cereal.

title: Coconut Cupcakes with Chocolate and Almonds
description: Tastes just like an Almond Joy.

ingredients.item: large eggs plus 4 egg whites, at room temperature
tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into pieces, at room temperature

instructions.text: Make the cupcakes: Position a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 325°. Line two 12-cup muffin pans with paper liners. Whisk the whole eggs and egg whites in a large bowl. Whisk in the cream of coconut and the coconut and vanilla extracts until smooth.

Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a large bowl. Beat in the butter, one piece at a time, with a mixer on low speed until the mixture resembles coarse meal, 3 to 4 minutes. Add half the egg mixture, increase the speed to medium-high and beat until fluffy, about 1 minute. Beat in the remaining egg mixture until combined, scraping down the bowl as needed.

Divide the batter among the prepared cups, filling each about halfway. Bake until a toothpick inserted into a cupcake comes out clean, 18 to 22 minutes. Let cool in the pans 10 minutes; transfer to racks to cool completely.

Make the topping: Combine the milk, coconut, confectioners' sugar, vanilla and salt in a medium saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat and cook until the milk is absorbed and the mixture thickens, stirring occasionally, about 15 minutes. Cool completely.

Make the glaze: Put the chocolate, corn syrup, butter and 3 tablespoons hot water in a microwave-safe bowl, cover with plastic wrap and microwave on 50 percent power until the chocolate melts, about 2 minutes. Whisk to combine. Keep warm.

Top each cupcake with a heaping tablespoonful of the coconut mixture, pressing gently until compact. Spoon 1 teaspoon glaze on top and garnish with 2 almonds. Refrigerate until the glaze sets, about 20 minutes.

title: Chocolate-Peanut Brittle Cupcakes
description: Tastes just like a Butterfinger.

ingredients.item: sticks unsalted butter, cut into pieces

instructions.text: Make the cupcakes: Position a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 300° using the convection setting, if available. Line two 12-cup muffin pans with paper liners. Put the butter, cocoa powder and 1/4 cup water in a microwave-safe bowl, cover with plastic wrap and microwave until the butter melts, about 2 minutes. Whisk to combine, then whisk in the brown sugar.

Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl. Whisk in the warm cocoa mixture. In another bowl, beat the buttermilk, eggs and vanilla; stir into the batter until just combined but don't overmix.

Divide the batter among the prepared cups, filling each three-quarters of the way. Bake until the cupcakes are slightly domed and spring back when lightly pressed, 25 to 30 minutes. Let cool in the pans 10 minutes, then transfer to racks to cool completely.

Make the brittle: Line a baking sheet with a silicone mat or parchment paper. Place the granulated sugar in a small saucepan over medium-high heat, bring to a boil and cook, swirling the pan but not stirring, until it turns amber. Remove from the heat; stir in the peanut butter and butterscotch chips until smooth. Immediately pour the mixture onto the prepared baking sheet, smooth into a thin layer with a spatula and let cool. Break the brittle into pieces, place in a resealable plastic bag and crush with a rolling pin.

Make the frosting: Bring the cream to a simmer in a small saucepan. Remove from the heat, add the peanut butter chips and let stand about 5 minutes. Whisk until smooth. Place the pan over a bowl of ice, stirring occasionally, until the frosting is spreadable, about 10 minutes. Spread on the cupcakes or transfer to a pastry bag with a large round tip and pipe on top; sprinkle with the brittle.

title: Peanut Cupcakes with Nougat-Chocolate Frosting
description: Tastes just like a Snickers.

ingredients.item: cups chopped salted roasted peanuts, plus more for garnish

instructions.text: Make the cupcakes: Position a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 350°. Line two 12-cup muffin pans with paper liners. Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt in a medium bowl.

In another bowl, beat the eggs and both sugars with a mixer until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes. Gradually beat in the melted butter and vanilla. With the mixer on low speed, add half of the flour mixture, the milk and then the remaining flour. Fold in the peanuts but don't overmix.

Divide the batter evenly among the prepared cups, filling each about halfway. Bake until a toothpick inserted into a cupcake comes out clean, 20 to 22 minutes. Let cool in the pans 10 minutes, then transfer to racks to cool completely.

Make the nougat frosting: Beat the marshmallow creme, peanut butter and salt with a mixer until smooth; set aside. Make the chocolate frosting: Put both chocolates in a large microwave-safe bowl and microwave on 50 percent power until soft, about 1 minute. Stir, then continue to microwave until melted, 1 to 2 more minutes. Add the confectioners' sugar, milk, butter, vanilla and salt and beat with a mixer until smooth and creamy.
Spread nougat frosting over each cupcake, then top with chocolate frosting, leaving some of the nougat exposed. Garnish with peanuts.

title: Bob's Oatmeal-Crusted Trout
source_note: Food Network Magazine, January/February 2010 - Fun Cooking
description: Chef Bob Iacovone's Irish-inspired fish recipe.
tips: I was inspired by Irish recipes, which often use oats for breading fish. You can also try this one with salmon. - Bob Iacovone

ingredients.item: kosher salt and freshly ground pepper

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 300°. Coarsely grind the oatmeal in a food processor. Transfer to a shallow dish and season with salt and pepper. Beat the egg and milk in another shallow dish.

Cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crisp, about 8 minutes. Transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate. Remove and reserve all but about 2 tablespoons drippings from the skillet. Add the leeks and garlic to the skillet and cook until tender, about 5 minutes. Add the parsley, bacon, and salt and pepper to taste; keep warm.

Line a baking sheet with a double layer of paper towels. Dredge the trout in the oats, dip in the milk mixture and then in the oats again, turning to coat. Heat the reserved bacon drippings with the olive oil in another large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the trout in batches until golden on one side, about 3 minutes, then flip and fry until cooked through, about 2 more minutes. Transfer to the prepared baking sheet and keep warm in the oven. Add the vinegar to the skillet and bring to a boil. Serve the trout with the leeks and drizzle with the vinegar dressing.

title: Claudia's Turkish Dumplings
source_note: Food Network Magazine, January/February 2010 - Fun Cooking
description: Traditional manti dumplings with yogurt sauce.
tips: I love manti, Turkish dumplings, with chili oil and yogurt. I thought it would be fun to try them with oatmeal! - Claudia Sidoti

ingredients.item: cups all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
small white onion, grated and squeezed dry

instructions.text: Make the dumplings: Cook the oatmeal as the label directs, then let cool. Combine the oatmeal, flour and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a bowl and make a well in the center. Add the egg and olive oil to the well and mix with a fork. Turn the dough out onto a floured surface and knead into a smooth ball. Cover with a towel and let rest 30 minutes. Meanwhile, mix the beef, onion, 1 tablespoon salt, and pepper to taste in a bowl and set aside.

Prepare the toppings: Whisk the yogurt, garlic, 1/2 cup water, and salt to taste in a bowl. Heat the olive oil in a small skillet over medium heat. Add the pepper flakes and paprika and cook 1 minute. Set the yogurt sauce and spiced oil aside.

Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Divide the dough into 4 pieces. On a floured surface, roll each piece into a 20-by-4-inch rectangle, then cut into 2-inch squares. Place 1 teaspoon beef filling in the center of each square, fold over into a triangle and press the edges to seal.
Boil the dumplings in batches, stirring occasionally, until they float, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain and transfer to bowls. Top with the yogurt sauce and spiced oil.

title: Almost-Famous Broccoli-Cheddar Soup
source_note: Food Network Magazine - Panera Bread knockoff recipe
description: Panera Bread wouldn't give up the recipe for its broccoli-cheddar soup, so Food Network Kitchens whipped up this rich, creamy knockoff.
tips: Panera Bread is famous for its broccoli-cheddar soup, but the real treat is that the soup comes in a sourdough bread bowl. More than 50 million cups and heads of broccoli have gone through this perfect imitation.

ingredients.item: kosher salt and freshly ground pepper
cups (about 8 ounces) grated extra-sharp white and yellow cheddar cheese, plus more for garnish

instructions.text: Melt the butter in a large Dutch oven or pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook until tender, about 5 minutes. Whisk in the flour and cook until golden, 3 to 4 minutes, then gradually whisk in the half-and-half until smooth. Add the chicken broth, bay leaves and nutmeg, then season with salt and pepper and bring to a simmer. Reduce the heat to medium-low and cook, uncovered, until thickened, about 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, prepare the bread bowls: Using a sharp knife, cut a circle into the top of each loaf, leaving a 1-inch border all around. Remove the bread top, then hollow out the middle with a fork or your fingers, leaving a thick bread shell.

Add the broccoli and carrot to the broth mixture and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes. Discard the bay leaves. Puree the soup in batches in a blender until smooth; you'll still have flecks of carrot and broccoli. Return to the pot. (Or puree the soup in the pot with an immersion blender.)
Add the cheese to the soup and whisk over medium heat until melted. Add up to 3/4 cup water if the soup is too thick. Ladle into the bread bowls and garnish with cheese.

title: How to Make Fresh Tomato Sauce
source_note: Cooking Light Magazine, March 2009 - Cooking Class
description: Fresh tomato sauce is a staple in Italy, where it's usually served with spaghetti.
tips: Fresh tomato sauce is a staple in Italy, where it's usually served with spaghetti. Although the sauce tastes rich and delicious, it only takes about 30 minutes to prepare. See recipe on page 138.
Pasta Primer: Learn about common pasta shapes and how to pair them with the proper sauce at CookingLight.com/features

instructions.text: To peel tomatoes, core and cut a small X through the skin on the bottom of tomatoes with a sharp knife. Place them in boiling water for about 30 seconds or just until skins begin to peel back. Quickly remove tomatoes from pan, and plunge them into ice water. Drain and remove skins. Cut each tomato in half lengthwise, and squeeze the juices and seeds into a colander over a bowl. Reserve tomato juices, and discard seeds. Finely chop tomatoes.
Heat extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add garlic, and cook just until it begins to brown lightly, taking care not to burn it.
Add tomatoes and reserved juices, and cook until almost all of the liquid evaporates.

Finish cooking the pasta with the sauce, which should be in a skillet large enough to combine the two and allow for tossing. Add enough of the pasta cooking water to the sauce to give the dish a creamy texture and marry the sauce to the pasta.

title: French Onion Burgers
description: Without Campbell's French Onion soup, it's just a hamburger.

ingredients.item: can (10 1/2 oz) Campbell's Condensed French Onion Soup
Pepperidge Farm Classic Sandwich Buns with Sesame Seeds, split

instructions.text: Shape beef into 4 (1/2-inch-thick) burgers.
Heat skillet over medium-high heat. Add burgers and cook until well browned on both sides. Remove burgers from skillet. Pour off fat.

Stir soup in skillet and heat to a boil. Return burgers to skillet. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 5 min. or until desired doneness. Top burgers with cheese and cook until cheese is melted. Serve burgers on buns with soup mixture for dipping.

title: Mini Peanut Butter Cupcakes
description: Tastes just like a Reese's Peanut Butter Cup.

ingredients.item: tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into pieces

instructions.text: Position a rack in the middle of the oven and preheat to 350°. Line a 24-cup mini muffin pan with paper liners. Combine the butter, cocoa powder and 1/4 cup water in a microwave-safe bowl, cover with plastic wrap and microwave until the butter melts, about 2 minutes. Whisk to combine, then whisk in the brown sugar.

Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl. Whisk in the warm cocoa mixture. In another bowl, whisk the buttermilk, egg and vanilla; stir into the batter until just combined but don't overmix.

Divide the batter among the prepared cups, filling each three-quarters of the way. Bake until the cupcakes spring back when touched, about 20 minutes. Let cool in the pan 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool completely.

Make the topping: Bring the cream to a simmer in a small saucepan, then pour over the peanut butter chips in a bowl and let stand about 5 minutes. Whisk until smooth. Refrigerate until the topping is set, about 10 minutes, then beat with a mixer until fluffy. Transfer to a pastry bag with a 1-inch round tip and pipe peaks onto each cupcake. Place in the freezer while you make the glaze.

Make the glaze: Put the butter, chocolate and 3 tablespoons hot water in a small, deep microwave-safe bowl, cover with plastic wrap and microwave on 50 percent power until the chocolate melts, about 2 minutes. Whisk until smooth. Dip the frozen peaks of each cupcake into the glaze, letting the excess drip off. Refrigerate until set, about 5 minutes.

title: Sarah's Oatmeal-Banana Parfaits
source_note: Food Network Magazine, January/February 2010 - Fun Cooking
description: A classic pudding with a twist using oatmeal-chocolate bark.
tips: This is like a classic pudding with a twist - I'm crumbing chocolate bark over whipped oatmeal cream. - Sarah

ingredients.item: 1-ounce packet plain instant oatmeal (about 1/3 cup) (oatmeal cream)

instructions.text: Make the bark: Preheat the oven to 350°. Combine the flour, oatmeal, walnuts, sugar and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Melt the butter in a pot over medium heat and cook until light brown, 6 minutes. Stir into the dry ingredients. Press the dough into the bottom of a 9-inch springform pan. Bake until golden brown, 30 minutes.
Remove the crust from the oven and sprinkle with the chocolate; let stand until soft, then spread with the back of a spoon. Refrigerate the bark until firm, 30 minutes. Break into pieces.

Make the oatmeal cream: Fill a large bowl with ice. Microwave 3/4 cup cream until simmering, 45 seconds. Puree with the oatmeal, sugar, a pinch of salt, vanilla and nutmeg in a blender. Transfer to a bowl and place over the ice; whisk until cool and thick. In another bowl, whisk the remaining 3/4 cup cream until soft peaks form; fold in the oatmeal puree.
Layer the oatmeal cream, bananas and crushed bark in 4 parfait glasses.

title: Low-Fat Scalloped Potatoes
source_note: Food Network Magazine, December 2010 - Lighten Up
description: We slimmed down the ultimate cold-weather side dish.
tips: Milk: Instead of cream, we used low-fat and whole milk and saved 13g fat per serving.

ingredients.item: tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more for the dish
pounds Yukon gold potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
cup low-fat milk (1%), at room temperature
cup whole milk, at room temperature

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 350°. Lightly butter a 3-quart baking dish. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil; add the potatoes and cook until just tender, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain the potatoes and return to the pot.

Meanwhile, melt 2 tablespoons butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the flour with a wooden spoon to make a paste. Cook, stirring, until the paste puffs slightly, about 1 minute. Gradually whisk in both milks and simmer, whisking constantly, until thickened, about 3 minutes. Remove from the heat and whisk in 1/2 teaspoon pepper, 1 1/2 teaspoons salt and the nutmeg. Pour the sauce over the potatoes and gently toss to coat.

Transfer the potato mixture to the prepared baking dish and sprinkle with the gruyère. Bake until heated through, about 10 minutes. Switch the oven to the broiler setting and broil the potatoes until browned on top, about 5 minutes. Let rest 10 minutes before serving.

title: Rice Krispies Nutty Butterscotch Squares
description: Golden raisins, dried apricots, butterscotch morsels and peanut butter combine in these tasty bars.
tips: Note: For best results, use fresh marshmallows.

ingredients.item: cups miniature marshmallows or 20 regular marshmallows

instructions.text: Combine Kellogg's Rice Krispies cereal, butterscotch morsels, raisins, apricots and pecans.
In medium saucepan melt butter over low heat. Add marshmallows and peanut butter. Stir until completely melted. Remove from heat. Stir in vanilla. Pour over cereal mixture. Stir until well coated.
Evenly press into 8 x 8 x 2-inch dish coated with cooking spray. Refrigerate 30 minutes. Cut into squares. Best if served the same day.

title: Double Chocolate Crackles
description: Chocolate cookies with crackled confectioners' sugar coating.
tips: Host a cookie swap with a theme: all chocolate, maybe?

instructions.text: Whisk the flour, granulated sugar, cocoa powder, baking powder and salt in a medium bowl. Whisk in the melted butter and eggs until combined, then stir in the white chocolate chips. Cover with plastic wrap and chill until firm, about 1 hour.

Preheat the oven to 350°. Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper. Put the confectioners' sugar in a shallow bowl. Roll tablespoonfuls of the dough into balls, then roll in the confectioners' sugar until well coated. Place 1 inch apart on the baking sheets.

Bake until the cookies are puffed and the tops are cracked, about 10 minutes. Let cool 2 minutes on the baking sheets, then transfer to a rack to cool completely. Store in an airtight container up to 1 week.

title: Mexican Chocolate Shortbread
description: Spiced chocolate shortbread with cinnamon and a hint of cayenne.

ingredients.item: tablespoons unsalted butter, softened, plus more for the pan
tablespoons sliced almonds, plus more for topping

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 350°. Butter a 9-inch-square metal baking pan, then line with parchment paper, leaving an overhang on all 4 sides. Pulse the flour, almonds, cocoa powder, cinnamon, salt and cayenne, if using, in a food processor until the almonds are finely ground.

Beat the butter and granulated sugar in a large bowl with a mixer until light and fluffy. Add the flour mixture and beat until just combined (the dough will be crumbly). Press the dough into the bottom of the prepared pan (you can cover the dough with plastic wrap and use the bottom of a measuring cup to even it out).

Prick the dough all over with a fork, then use a sharp knife to cut it into 18 strips. Top with almonds, lightly pressing them in. Sprinkle with the raw sugar. Refrigerate until the dough is firm, about 10 minutes.

Bake until the shortbread is slightly puffed and firm, 30 to 35 minutes. Remove the pan from the oven and immediately retrace the strips with a knife; cool completely in the pan on a rack. Lift up the parchment paper to remove the shortbread from the pan, then separate into bars. Store in an airtight container up to 1 week.

title: Glazed Vegetables
description: Simple glazed carrots and celery with butter and sugar.

ingredients.item: each sliced carrots and celery stalks

instructions.text: Cook 4 each sliced carrots and celery stalks in salted boiling water, 5 minutes. Add 1 1/2 cups frozen pearl onions; cook 1 more minute, then drain.
Cook 2 tablespoons each butter and sugar, and the juice from 1/2 lemon in a skillet until syrupy. Toss in the vegetables and season with salt and pepper.

title: Rice Pilaf with Cranberries
description: Wild rice with dried cranberries and almonds.

ingredients.item: cups wild rice blend in chicken broth with 1/2 cinnamon stick
minced onion in a skillet with 3 tablespoons butter

instructions.text: Cook 1 1/2 cups wild rice blend in chicken broth with 1/2 cinnamon stick as the label directs.

Cook 1/4 cup minced onion in a skillet with 3 tablespoons butter, 5 minutes. Add 1/4 cup sliced almonds and cook 2 minutes. Add 1/4 cup dried cranberries and cook 2 more minutes. Toss with the rice. Top with chopped parsley.

title: Cheddar-Chive Turnovers
description: Quick appetizer turnovers with cheddar and chives.

ingredients.item: tablespoons melted butter with a pinch of salt and cayenne

instructions.text: Mix 3 tablespoons melted butter with a pinch of salt and cayenne.

Lay out rounds of refrigerated biscuit dough on a parchment paper-lined baking sheet. Brush with the butter; top with shredded cheddar and chopped chives. Fold into half-moons and crimp to seal, then bake as the label directs. Brush with more butter.

title: White Chili with Quick-Roasted Garlic
description: Creamy white bean chili with quick-roasted garlic - Melissa's secret weapon.

ingredients.item: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ounce box frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
cup grated monterey jack cheese, for garnish

instructions.text: Make the roasted garlic: Toss the 12 cloves garlic with the olive oil and 1 tablespoon water in a microwave-safe bowl. Cover with a wet paper towel and microwave until soft, about 90 seconds. Let cool slightly, then squeeze the cloves out of the skins. Set aside.

Prepare the chili: Preheat the broiler. Cook the shallots in the butter in a large saucepan over medium-low heat until caramelized, about 20 minutes. Meanwhile, place the chiles on a foil-lined broiler pan and broil, turning, about 8 minutes. Peel the peppers and chop.
Add the minced garlic to the shallots and cook until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Add the flour and cook, stirring, until toasted, about 3 minutes.

Meanwhile, squeeze the soft pulp from the roasted garlic cloves into the pan. Add the string broth, chicken, beans, and next 4 ingredients through cilantro. Bring to a simmer and cook until thickened, about 30 minutes, adding the chili and spinach during the last 10 minutes. Add the cream and season with salt and pepper.

tips: Melissa's secret weapon: Quick-roasted garlic in the microwave gives all the flavor in a fraction of the time.

title: Asian Chicken Salad
source_note: Food Network Magazine - Fast Food Makeover
description: A healthy makeover of KFC's two-piece meal, converting it to a satisfying Asian salad with 80% less fat.

ingredients.item: KFC Breast (with corn, coleslaw and a biscuit)

instructions.text: Discard the chicken skin and shred the meat from a KFC Breast and a biscuit.
Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, brown sugar, ginger, garlic, red pepper flakes, and sesame oil. Toss the chicken with the cabbage, carrot, and cilantro.
Cut the biscuit into cubes and toss with the salad. Drizzle with the dressing. Toast sesame seeds and sprinkle over the salad.

tips: The makeover cuts the fat by 80 percent, while keeping the Colonel's secret herbs and spices.
Original KFC meal had 47 grams of fat—almost an entire day's worth.

title: Garlicky Broccoli Rabe
source_note: Cooking Light Magazine, March 2009 - Dinner Party Menu
description: Broccoli rabe's bitterness is a pleasant foil to the sweet spices in lamb dishes.

instructions.text: Cook 8 cups (2-inch) cut broccoli rabe in boiling water 2 minutes or until crisp-tender. Drain and plunge into ice water; drain.

Heat 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil and 1 tablespoon butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add 1/2 teaspoon crushed red pepper and 4 minced garlic cloves; cook 1 minute, stirring frequently.
Add broccoli rabe and 1/2 teaspoon salt; cook 3 minutes or until heated, stirring occasionally. Serve with lemon wedges.

tips: Pour the same wine you used for the lamb dish. You can make the cookies a couple of days in advance.

title: Albuquerque Turkey
description: Southwest-style turkey with green chiles and tomatoes, blended smooth for a flavorful sauce.

ingredients.item: ounce bag frozen pepper stir-fry (such as Birds Eye)
ounce can chopped green chiles, drained
teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, divided
pound boneless, skinless chicken breast (or ground turkey tenderloin, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces)

instructions.text: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add pepper stir-fry to pan; saute 5 minutes. Add carrots; saute, stirring occasionally. Add 4 cups water, tomato paste, broth, and tomatoes; bring to a boil. Drop in meat mixture (about 45 meatballs) into boiling liquid; bring to simmer 30 seconds or until blended. Bring broth mixture to a boil in a food processor; process 30 seconds.

Place one-third of broth mixture in blender lid (to allow steam to escape); blend 15 minutes or until tender. Add remaining 4 teaspoons oil, carrots, chiles and broth. Stir in salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer 45 minutes or until thickened.

Combine broth, chicken, and next 6 ingredients (through sambal). Whisk 1 teaspoon oil, chicken, and remaining 1 teaspoon salt. Reduce heat, and simmer 15 minutes, stirring until meatballs are done. Stir in remaining 1/4 cup cilantro and 1/2 teaspoon pepper.

tips: Combine with chicken, pork, or seafood. Serve with remaining broth mixture. Add 1/4 cup rice, cilantro, 1/4 teaspoon salt.

title: Broccoli and Chicken Noodle Soup
description: A healthier version of creamy chicken noodle soup with broccoli and Velveeta Light cheese.

ingredients.item: ounces uncooked vermicelli, broken into 2-inch pieces
cups (8 ounces) shredded light processed cheese (such as Velveeta Light)

instructions.text: Heat a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Coat pan with cooking spray. Add onion, mushrooms, and garlic to pan; saute 5 minutes or until liquid evaporates, stirring occasionally. Reduce heat to medium; add butter to mushroom mixture, stirring until butter melts. Sprinkle mushroom mixture with flour; cook 2 minutes, stirring occasionally. Gradually add milk and broth, stirring constantly with a whisk; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low; cook 10 minutes or until slightly thick, stirring constantly.

Add pasta to pan; cook 10 minutes. Add cheese to pan, and stir until cheese melts. Add chicken and remaining ingredients to pan; cook 5 minutes or until broccoli is tender and soup is thoroughly heated.

tips: If the broccoli florets are large, break into smaller pieces at the stalk instead of chopping them; they'll cook more quickly.
Count on having dinner on the table in about 40 minutes, and serve this soup the moment it's done for the best results.
If you have leftovers, you will want to thin the soup with a little chicken broth or milk to the desired consistency.

title: How to Make Fresh Tomato Sauce
source_note: Cooking Light Magazine, March 2009 - Cooking Class
description: Fresh tomato sauce is a staple in Italy. Although the sauce tastes rich and delicious, it only takes about 30 minutes to prepare.

instructions.text: To peel tomatoes, core and cut a small X through the skin on the bottom of tomatoes with a sharp knife. Place them in boiling water for about 30 seconds or just until skins begin to peel back. Quickly remove tomatoes from pan, and plunge them into ice water. Drain and remove skins. Cut each tomato in half lengthwise, and squeeze the juices and seeds into a colander over a bowl. Reserve tomato juices, and discard seeds. Finely chop tomatoes.
Heat extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add garlic, and cook just until it begins to brown lightly, taking care not to burn it.
Add tomatoes and reserved juices, and cook until almost all of the liquid evaporates.

Finish cooking the pasta with the sauce, which should be in a skillet large enough to combine the two and allow for tossing. Add enough of the pasta cooking water to the sauce to give the dish a creamy texture and marry the sauce to the pasta.

tips: Learn about common pasta shapes and how to pair them with the proper sauce at CookingLight.com/features

title: Ravioli with Herbed Ricotta Filling
description: You can shape the pasta and freeze it up to a month before cooking.

ingredients.item: cup (1 ounce) grated fresh Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese
cup (1 ounce) shaved fresh Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese

instructions.text: To prepare ravioli, place ricotta in a cheesecloth-lined colander; drain 30 minutes. Combine ricotta, 1/4 cup Parmigiano-Reggiano, and next 4 ingredients (through egg), stirring until well combined.

Place 1 (5 x 3-inch) Classic Pasta Dough sheet on a lightly floured surface. Spoon 1 1/2 teaspoons filling mixture 1 1/2 inches from left edge in the center of sheet. Spoon 1 1/2 teaspoons filling mixture at 3-inch intervals along the length of the sheet. Moisten edges and in between each filling portion with water; place 1 (5 x 3-inch) pasta sheet on top, pressing to seal. Cut pasta sheet crosswise into 3 (3 x 3-inch) ravioli, trimming edges with a sharp knife or pastry wheel. Place ravioli on a lightly floured baking sheet (cover with a damp towel to prevent drying). Repeat procedure with remaining pasta sheets and filling mixture to form 20 ravioli.

Bring 6 quarts water and salt to a boil in an 8-quart pot. Add half of ravioli to pot; cook 1 1/2 minutes or until no longer translucent. Remove ravioli from water with a slotted spoon. Repeat procedure with remaining ravioli.

To prepare sauce, heat oil in a large skillet over low heat. Add garlic to pan; cook 6 minutes or until garlic is tender. Remove from heat. Place 5 ravioli in each of a shallow bowls; drizzle each serving with 1 1/2 teaspoons garlic oil. Top each serving with 1 tablespoon basil and 1 tablespoon shaved Parmigiano-Reggiano. Serve immediately.

tips: Use a sharp knife or a pasta wheel to cut the sheets crosswise into ravioli. Serve with a delicate sauce, and allow the pasta to be the star.

title: Halibut with Coconut-Red Curry Sauce
source_note: Cooking Light Magazine, March 2009 - Dinner Tonight (30 minutes)
description: A bed of seasoned rice with bok choy soaks up the sauce.
servings_yield: 4 servings (serving size: 1 fillet and about 1/3 cup sauce)

ingredients.item: cups water and 3/4 cup basmati rice in a medium saucepan

instructions.text: Combine 2 1/2 cups water and 3/4 cup basmati rice in a medium saucepan; bring to a boil. Cover, reduce heat, and simmer 12 minutes. Stir in 2 cups chopped baby bok choy; cover and cook 8 minutes or until liquid is absorbed. Combine 1 1/2 tablespoons low-sodium soy sauce, 1 tablespoon fresh lime juice, 1/2 teaspoon sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon dark sesame oil; stir into rice mixture.

Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add fish to pan; cook 5 minutes on each side or until fish flakes easily when tested with a fork or until desired degree of doneness. Remove fish from pan; keep warm.

Add remaining 1 teaspoon oil to pan. Add onion, green onions, and ginger; saute 2 minutes. Stir in coconut milk and the next 4 ingredients (through coriander). Bring to a boil; cook 1 minute. Remove from heat. Stir in basil and juice.

tips: Prepare salad up to a day ahead (it's great for lunch). Sprinkle nuts on just before serving.

title: Spicy Asian Noodles with Chicken
source_note: Cooking Light Magazine, March 2009 - Dinner Tonight (30 minutes)
description: Add a snow pea saute to complete the meal.

ingredients.item: cups chopped roasted skinless, boneless chicken breasts
teaspoons sambal oelek (ground fresh chile paste)

instructions.text: Heat 2 teaspoons oil in a small skillet over medium-high heat. Add ginger and garlic to pan; cook 45 seconds, stirring constantly. Place in a large bowl. Stir in remaining 1 teaspoon oil, chicken, and next 6 ingredients (through sambal).
Cook noodles according to package directions. Drain and rinse under cold water. Cut noodles into smaller pieces. Add noodles to bowl; toss well to coat. Sprinkle with peanuts.

tips: Heat 2 teaspoons canola oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add 2 minced garlic cloves; saute 15 seconds. Add 2 cups trimmed snow peas and 1 cup drained sliced water chestnuts; saute 3 minutes or until crisp-tender. Remove from heat; stir in 1 tablespoon low-sodium soy sauce.

title: Tomato-Ricotta Spaghetti
description: Roasting tomatoes intensifies their sweetness. We also tested this recipe with grated Parmigiano-Reggiano - it's a splurge that makes the difference.

ingredients.item: cup (2 ounces) ricotta salata cheese, crumbled

instructions.text: Place tomatoes on a foil-lined baking sheet. Drizzle with 1 teaspoon oil; sprinkle with 1/4 teaspoon salt. Bake at 400° for 20 minutes or until tomatoes collapse.

Cook pasta according to package directions, omitting salt and fat. Drain pasta in a colander over a bowl, reserving 1/3 cup cooking liquid. Return pasta and reserved liquid to pan; stir in tomatoes, remaining 4 teaspoons oil, remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt, basil, pepper, and cheese. Toss well. Serve immediately.

tips: Get the most flavor: Use cooking techniques that intensify the taste of foods. Roasting tomatoes for Tomato-Ricotta Spaghetti boosts their sweetness and helps the dish to shine. The same principle applies to the sauteed tomato paste and roasted peppers in Sausage and Roasted Pepper Pasta (page 164).

title: Zinfandel-Braised Leg of Lamb
description: Reducing the wine before placing it in the slow cooker gives a more rounded flavor.

ingredients.item: teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, divided
cup zinfandel or other light red wine
cups hot cooked egg noodles (about 4 1/2 cups uncooked pasta)

instructions.text: Unroll lamb; trim fat. Sprinkle evenly with 1/2 teaspoon salt and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Reroll lamb; secure at 1-inch intervals with twine. Sprinkle evenly with flour. Heat oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add lamb to pan; cook 6 minutes, turning to brown on all sides. Place lamb in an electric slow cooker. Add juniper berries, allspice, and garlic to pan; cook over medium heat 2 minutes or until garlic lightly browned. Add wine to pan, scraping pan to loosen browned bits; cook until reduced to 1/2 cup (about 3 minutes).
Scrape wine mixture into cooker; add basil and bay leaves. Cover and cook on LOW 8 hours or until lamb is tender.
Remove lamb from cooker; keep warm. Strain cooking liquid through a sieve; discard solids.

tips: Stay safe: Don't add frozen food to the slow cooker or use the cooker to defrost food - always defrost in the refrigerator or microwave. In a cooker, thawing food will linger too long between 40° and 140°, leaving it vulnerable to bacterial contamination. For the same reason, don't reheat food in the cooker.

title: Borlotti Minestrone
source_note: Cooking Light Magazine, March 2009 - Food Trend: Heirloom Beans
description: Borlotti beans - the Italian variety of cranberry beans - can be ordered from www.ranchogordo.com, among other online retailers.
servings_yield: 8 servings (serving size: 1 1/4 cups soup and 1 tablespoon cheese)

ingredients.item: cup (2 ounces) grated fresh Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese

instructions.text: Sort and wash beans; place in a large bowl. Cover with water to 2 inches above beans; cover and let stand 8 hours or overnight. Drain beans.
Place beans in a large saucepan, and cover with water to 3 inches above beans; bring to a boil. Reduce heat; simmer 1 1/2 hours or until tender. Drain.

Heat a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add bacon to pan; cook 6 minutes or until crisp, stirring frequently. Add onion and next 5 ingredients (through garlic); saute 4 minutes. Add zucchini; saute 3 minutes. Add kale; saute 2 minutes or until kale wilts. Add 3 cups water, tomato paste, broth, and tomatoes; bring to a boil. Cover, reduce heat, and simmer 30 minutes. Add beans; simmer, uncovered, 30 minutes. Stir in salt and pepper; sprinkle with cheese.

tips: Why are time-honored varieties of beans finding fresh flavor in home kitchens? 'I think heirloom beans taste better,' says Steve Sando, whose Rancho Gordo in Napa, California, grows and sells nearly 30 varieties of distinctive beans. 'Runner beans tend to be buttery. Christmas limas have a distinct chestnut taste, and the bean broth is beefy. Some types are like potatoes in texture; others are creamy. They are not bred for uniform growth, uniform size, or disease resistance. They've been saved from extinction because they taste good.'

Pressure cookers and induction burners: Both can help you get meals on the table quickly and efficiently. Modern pressure cookers are safer than their predecessors and significantly reduce cooking time, a boon for harried home cooks.

title: Barley and Beef Soup
description: Make this soup the night before to allow time for its flavors to develop. Pour hot servings into a thermos to take for lunch, or reheat individual portions in the microwave as needed. Serve the soup with crusty bread, crackers, or Spicy Whole-Wheat Pita Chips (page 90).

ingredients.item: pound chuck steak, trimmed and cut into 1/2-inch cubes

instructions.text: Heat a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Coat pan with cooking spray. Add chopped onion and beef to pan; cook 10 minutes or until onion is tender and beef is browned, stirring occasionally. Add chopped carrot and chopped celery to pan; cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Stir in garlic; cook 30 seconds. Stir in barley and remaining ingredients, and bring to a boil. Cover, reduce heat, and simmer 40 minutes or until the barley is done and vegetables are tender. Discard bay leaves.

tips: Make dishes ahead when possible. Barley and Beef Soup (above), like many soups and stews, improves with time; make it the night before. Lemony Hummus (page 90), too, will grow better as its ingredients marry.

Keep it separate. To prevent soggy sandwiches, pack separate zip-top bags of tomato slices, lettuce, and bread, then assemble the sandwiches just before serving. Similarly, don't dress leafy salads until you are ready to eat. Salt will draw moisture out of watery ingredients, so add items such as tomatoes and cucumbers to a grain salad at the last minute for the best results.

Put leftovers to good use. Consider applying extras from dinner to the next day's lunch. Slice leftover chicken or beef and serve it on top of pasta or salad greens, mix it into a grain salad (see Tabbouleh with Chicken and Red Pepper, page 86), or make it into a sandwich. Chop extra grilled vegetables and add them to soups, salads, or sandwiches.

Stay safe. Keep cold food cold (below 40°) and hot food hot (above 140°) as it travels. Use insulated lunch bags, coolers, thermoses, ice bags, and frozen gel packs to help with temperature control. If reheating items in a microwave, the United States Department of Agriculture recommends they reach 165° and are served steaming hot.

title: Yale College Punch
source_note: Food Network Magazine - Punch: The Delights (and Dangers) of the Flowing Bowl by David Wondrich
description: This recipe from 1867 is much more doable for modern-day spirit lovers. It's the 19th-century version of that college favorite 'jungle juice.'

instructions.text: In a large punch bowl, steep 1 cup pineapple chunks in 750 ml cognac for an hour or two in the refrigerator.
Add 2 1/2 cups seltzer or club soda and 1/4 cup superfine sugar, stirring until the sugar is dissolved, then add between 375 ml and 750 ml cold demi-sec champagne.

tips: Punch is back in style. Retro cocktails get all the attention these days, but punch predates individual mixed drinks by at least two centuries.
Some of the punches call for far-out ingredients like whale cholesterol, but this recipe from 1867 is much more doable.

title: Reduced-Sugar Banana Bread with Truvia Natural Sweetener
description: Sprinkle sweetness on your holidays without feeling like a calorie grinch.

ingredients.item: cup (about 2 medium) very ripe bananas, mashed

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°. Spray 9x5x3-inch loaf pan with non-stick spray.
Whisk together the flour, Truvia natural sweetener, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl. Set aside.
Mix the mashed bananas, buttermilk, egg, butter and vanilla in a medium bowl.
Lightly fold the banana mixture into the dry ingredients until just combined. The batter will be thick and chunky. Don't overmix or your loaf will be small and tough.
Scrape the batter into the loaf pan. Bake about 55 minutes, until golden brown and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes; transfer to wire rack.

tips: *May substitute with 12 packets Truvia natural sweetener

title: Chocolate Crepes Sweetened with Truvia Natural Sweetener

instructions.text: Assemble all ingredients.
In a large bowl, combine flour, Truvia natural sweetener and salt.
Add milk, melted butter, eggs, cocoa powder and vanilla; whisk mixture until very smooth.
Place batter in fridge for 1 hour to allow flour to absorb liquid.
Place skillet or crepe pan over medium heat; heat until hot.
Spray pan with non-stick cooking spray.
Pour 1/4 cup batter in pan and swirl to form thin layer.
Cook for about 1 minute or until golden brown on the bottom; flip and cook other side for 30 seconds.
Place cooked crepe on a towel; cool for about 2 minutes.
Stack crepes with wax paper between each layer to prevent sticking.

tips: Serving Suggestion: Place several rows of fresh or frozen raspberries down the center of the crepe and fold in half. Dust with chocolate shavings and powdered sugar. Additional ingredients may include strawberries, banana slices, fruit sauce or light whipped toppings.

title: Grape Turkey Chili
description: Try this delicious, comforting dish with packed with antioxidant power. For a heartier meal, stir in a can or two of drained cannellini beans. Serve over warm polenta or rice, in taco shells, or in tortillas.

ingredients.item: cups Welch's 100% Grape Juice made from Concord grapes
teaspoon mild chili powder (or to taste)
chopped red onion, chopped cilantro, low-fat sour cream, for garnish

instructions.text: In a large pot, cook the onion in the oil over medium heat until softened, about 8 minutes. Add the garlic to the pot; cook 1 minute. Add the turkey and cook, stirring often to break up the lumps, until lightly browned.
Stir in the tomato sauce, grape juice, chili powder, oregano, cumin, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer. Cook 20 minutes or until thickened.
Serve hot topped with red onion, cilantro, and sour cream.

tips: Welch's 100% Grape Juice releases tons of amazing antioxidants called polyphenols, which fight free-radicals to help prevent cell damage. By the glass, or in your favorite recipe, you just can't beat the power of purple.
An Antioxidant Punch: Color counts. Its deep purple color is your first clue that our juice packs a powerful punch. The deeper and darker the color of the produce, the higher the antioxidant power.
Heart Healthy: Years of research shows that Welch's Grape Juice made from Concord grapes helps protect cardiovascular health.

title: Raisin Fudge Pecan Pie
description: A rich chocolate pecan pie made with California raisins.

instructions.text: Heat oven to 350°F. In small saucepan, combine chocolate chips and syrup. Cook until chips are melted and mixture is smooth. Stir in half-and-half. In large bowl, combine chocolate mixture and eggs; beat until smooth. Stir in pecans and raisins.

Pour into pie shell. Bake at 350°F for 40 to 40 minutes or until top is set and knife inserted in center comes out clean. Cool completely. Store in refrigerator. Top with whipped cream and sprinkle with cocoa, if desired.

title: Applesauce Bread Pudding
description: A comforting bread pudding made with applesauce and California raisins.

ingredients.item: loaf (16 ounces) sliced light-style white bread

instructions.text: Cut bread into 1/2-inch cubes. Toss with raisins and cinnamon in a large bowl. In another bowl, beat together milk, applesauce, egg whites, sugar and vanilla. Pour mixture over bread cubes and let stand 25 minutes.

Heat oven to 350°F. Spray an 8-inch square baking pan with nonstick cooking spray. Pour bread mixture into prepared pan and bake 35 to 40 minutes or until a knife inserted in the center comes out clean. Remove from oven. Let cool 15 to 20 minutes and serve.

title: Meringue Swirls
source_note: Food Network Magazine, December 2010 - Holiday Cookie Plate
description: Give this year's holiday cookie plate a new spin with one of these beauties.

ingredients.item: large egg whites, at room temperature
vanilla bean, split lengthwise (or use 1/4 teaspoon vanilla extract)
Coarse sugar crystals and/or silver nonpareils, for sprinkling

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 250°. Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper. Beat the egg whites and salt in a large bowl with a mixer on medium speed until frothy (use the whisk attachment if using a stand mixer). Add the cream of tartar; increase the speed to medium-high and add the superfine sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time. Scrape the seeds from the vanilla bean into the meringue (or add the extract) and continue beating until the sugar is dissolved and the meringue is thick, glossy and forms stiff peaks, about 6 minutes.
Fit a piping bag with a large star tip. Fill the bag with the meringue and pipe spirals on the prepared baking sheets, about 1 inch apart. Sprinkle with the coarse sugar.
Bake 1 hour, then turn off the oven and let the meringues stand in the oven until dry, about 2 hours. Store in an airtight container up to 1 week.

title: Golden Sesame Roll-Ups
source_note: Food Network Magazine, December 2010 - Holiday Cookie Plate
description: Give this year's holiday cookie plate a new spin with one of these beauties.

ingredients.item: to 9-ounce sheet frozen puff pastry, thawed (half of a box)

instructions.text: Mix the sugar, sesame seeds and cinnamon in a small bowl. Lay out a 12-by-16-inch piece of parchment paper. Sprinkle 1/2 cup of the sugar mixture evenly on the paper. Lay the puff pastry on top and sprinkle with another 1/2 cup of the sugar mixture. Roll out the dough into a 12-inch square, pressing the sugar into the dough with the rolling pin. Roll up the dough tightly into a log. Wrap in the parchment paper and freeze until firm, about 30 minutes.

Preheat the oven to 350°. Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper. Slice the log into 1/2-inch-thick rounds and place 1 inch apart on the prepared baking sheets. (If the spirals unravel, pinch them back together.) Freeze until firm, about 20 minutes.

Bake until the pastry is puffed and light brown, 10 to 15 minutes. Remove from the oven and sprinkle with the remaining sugar mixture. Return to the oven and bake until the cookies are glazed and golden, 10 to 15 more minutes. Use a spatula to transfer the warm cookies to another sheet of parchment paper, flipping them over before the sugar hardens. Let cool completely. Store in an airtight container up to 1 week.

title: Chocolate Mousse Torte
source_note: Kraft/Jell-O Advertisement - 'Twas the night to remember
description: An elegant no-bake chocolate mousse torte with Nilla wafers, Jell-O pudding, Cool Whip, and Philadelphia cream cheese.

ingredients.item: pkg. (3.9 oz. each) JELL-O Chocolate Instant Pudding
cups plus 2 Tbsp. cold milk, divided
tub (8 oz.) COOL WHIP Whipped Topping, thawed, divided
pkg. (8 oz.) PHILADELPHIA Cream Cheese, softened

instructions.text: STAND 16 wafers around inside edge of 9-inch round pan lined with plastic wrap. Melt 3 chocolate squares as directed on package.
BEAT pudding mixes and 2 cups milk in medium bowl with whisk 2 min. Add melted chocolate; mix well. Stir in 1 cup COOL WHIP; pour into prepared pan.
BEAT cream cheese, sugar and remaining COOL WHIP; spread over pudding. Top with remaining wafers. Refrigerate 3 hours. Meanwhile, shave remaining chocolate square into curls.
INVERT torte onto plate. Remove pan and plastic wrap. Top torte with remaining COOL WHIP, berries and chocolate curls.
